cards.title: Ideal infinite-blockade Rydberg CZ Hamiltonian
cards.role: Defines the ideal gate trajectory whose fidelity susceptibility is reproduced.

checks.reason: Hamiltonian is explicit in Eq. (12).
Each |1><r| term is paired with its Hermitian conjugate; projecting out |rr> preserves Hermiticity.

cards.numerical_form: 8x8 dense Hamiltonian in the {|0>,|1>,|r>} tensor basis with |rr> omitted.

cards.title: Sinusoidal time-optimal control phase

source_refs.value: Main text: parameterized sinusoidal phase modulation, citing Ref. 8
Evered et al., Nature 622, 268-272 (2023), Methods: A/(2pi)=0.1122, omega/Omega=1.0431, phi0=-0.7318, delta0=0, Omega*T/(2pi)=1.215

cards.role: Defines a reconstructed direct-integration diagnostic; the current paper does not disclose that these cited generic-pulse parameters are the exact Fig. 15 trajectory.

checks.reason: The current paper cites the sinusoidal protocol and the primary source prints a generic parameter set; target-specific identity with the Fig. 15 trajectory remains unverified.
A and phi0 are dimensionless; omega and delta0 have angular-frequency units; Omega*T is dimensionless.

cards.numerical_form: phase(t, params), with Omega=1 normalized units and T=2*pi*1.215.
open_questions: What exact phase trajectory and optimizer output generated the paper's Fig. 15 curves?

cards.title: Haar-averaged fidelity response

source_refs.value: Eq. (9) and Appendix Eq. (G7), source label eq:response_avg

cards.role: Maps the ideal gate trajectory and a noise operator to the universal response.

checks.reason: The finite-subspace Haar average is explicit in Appendix Eq. (G7).
Expanding A(f)=integral exp(i2pi f t)O_H(t)dt gives the same double integral and cosine kernel.

cards.numerical_form: Fourier-transform O_H(t), then evaluate Tr[A A^dag P]/D - (Tr[A P A^dag P]+|Tr[A P]|^2)/(D(D+1)).

cards.title: Frequency and relative-intensity noise operators
cards.role: Defines the two perturbations used in Fig. 6 and Fig. 15.

checks.reason: Both operators are explicit in Eqs. (13)-(14).
Projectors are Hermitian and the intensity coupling includes its Hermitian conjugate.

cards.title: Universal response scaling

source_refs.value: Eqs. (15)-(16), source labels Eq:nu_scaling and Eq:I_Scaling

cards.role: Turns Fig. 15 universal curves into the dimensional responses of Fig. 6(a).

checks.reason: Scaling laws are explicit in Eqs. (15)-(16).
Two time integrals yield Omega^-2 for O_nu; the Omega factor in each O_I cancels both time factors.

cards.numerical_form: x=f_MHz/rabi_MHz; I_nu in MHz^-2 equals g_nu(x)/(2*pi*rabi_MHz)^2, and I_I=g_I(x).

cards.title: Appendix-L response fits

source_refs.value: Appendix L, four six-parameter fits for Haar and symmetric-Haar frequency/intensity responses

cards.role: Defines the paper-exact analytic envelope target because all four approximate-fit coefficient sets are printed in the paper.

checks.reason: All coefficients are printed in Appendix L.
Both fit families decay toward zero at large normalized frequency, matching the filter-response limit.

cards.numerical_form: appendix_fit(normalized_frequency, metric, noise_kind), used to generate the final Fig. 15 response and the Fig. 6(a) rescaling.

cards.title: FRT error-budget contributions

source_refs.value: Main text around Fig. 7 and Appendix D: decay, motion, and 0.8% shot-to-shot intensity noise

cards.role: Generates the theoretical error-source curves in Fig. 1(f), Fig. 7, and the infidelity part of Figs. 9 and 12.

checks.reason: Appendix D prints the symmetric-Haar coefficient 2.6 and the measured 78 us and 166 us decay lifetimes.
Frequency and motion terms approach Omega^-2 for low-frequency noise; decay approaches Omega^-1 and DC intensity noise approaches Omega^0.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the Appendix-L response at zero frequency to obtain quasistatic frequency/intensity coefficients, add the lifetime-derived decay term, and expose all unavailable PSD or Doppler variances as explicit inputs. No source-figure pixels are computational inputs.
open_questions: The measured PSD arrays and Doppler variance were not released, so their absolute paper-specific contributions remain blocked until a public numerical source is found.

cards.title: Fixed-power principal-quantum-number scaling

source_refs.value: Saffman, Walker, and Molmer, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 2313 (2010)

cards.role: Reconstructs the mechanisms and optimum in Fig. 8 at fixed laser power.

checks.reason: The paper states Omega/(2pi)=7.7 MHz at n=61, approximately 13 MHz at n=44, and an optimum at n=44.
The decay contribution decreases with n while frequency and electric-field sensitivities increase, forcing an interior optimum.

cards.numerical_form: Use the two Rabi-frequency anchors printed in the text and expose lifetime/electric-field scaling assumptions as parameters. Only the anchor-constrained Rabi curve is paper-specific; unavailable author arrays are never inferred from figure pixels.
open_questions: The exact lifetime and electric-field-noise arrays used by the authors are not published.

cards.title: Cited CZ gate protocol controls

source_refs.value: Levine et al., PRL 123, 170503 (2019): Delta/Omega=0.377371, xi=3.90242, Omega*tau=4.29268
Fromonteil et al., PRX Quantum 4, 020335 (2023): resonant pulse sequences and Protocol II
Evered et al., Nature 622, 268 (2023): sinusoidal time-optimal control

cards.role: Defines the three independent gate trajectories compared in Fig. 9.

checks.reason: The three primary sources print the pulse parameters or pulse areas used here; target-paper identity of the Fromonteil variant remains explicitly reconstructed.
The cited sources derive computational-subspace closure and the controlled phase for the printed segment products; the implementation will add an independent numerical closure check.

cards.numerical_form: Piecewise-constant protocol segments plus the existing sinusoidal protocol, all propagated in the same infinite-blockade eight-dimensional Hilbert space.
open_questions: The target paper does not name which Fromonteil sequence variant was plotted; Protocol II is inferred from the zero-frequency response and will remain disclosed as reconstructed identity.

cards.title: Rydberg spin-lock response

source_refs.value: Appendix H, analytic prediction of the Rydberg spin-lock experiment

cards.role: Reproduces the analytical component of Fig. 10 and verifies the PSD-to-decay-rate mapping.

checks.reason: At long time the sinc-squared response approaches a delta function centered at f=Omega/(2pi).
The finite Rydberg lifetime contributes the printed Gamma_Ryd/2 floor.

cards.numerical_form: Numerically evaluate the finite-time sinc-squared filter and the lifetime floor. Mapping it to an absolute decay-rate curve requires a public numerical PSD and is therefore blocked for the paper-specific panel.
open_questions: The author PSD array is unavailable, so the paper-specific absolute spin-lock curve cannot be calculated independently.

cards.title: Seven-qubit many-body fidelity response

source_refs.value: Fig. 11 caption: seven qubits, 7.7 MHz quench, 6 us duration, and tangent detuning sweep

cards.role: Defines the quench and quasi-adiabatic response functions in Fig. 11.

checks.reason: All Pauli, number, and density-density terms are Hermitian.
The Hamiltonian, system size, duration, quench Rabi frequency, and detuning endpoints are explicit in the main text and Fig. 11 caption.

cards.numerical_form: Exact 2^7 state-vector propagation with tangent equations for cosine and sine perturbations at every sampled frequency.
open_questions: The atom spacing, C6 value, and exact ramp schedules are not tabulated; the generated target is therefore an exploratory reconstruction.

cards.title: SSB phase-flip and depolarizing proxy model

source_refs.value: Appendix D, abstract analytical models and Fig. 17

cards.role: Reproduces Fig. 17 and the theoretical sensitivity mechanism underlying Fig. 16(b).

checks.reason: Appendix D prints both state-averaged phase-flip fidelities and the first-order SSB slope formula.
At p=0 the circuit-inferred infidelity reduces to the symmetric depolarizing infidelity 3d/4.
At d=0 the first-order p contribution cancels; the remaining inferred error is quadratic in p.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the paper equations over the printed p and d ranges and fit the same panel-wise linear slopes.
open_questions: The exact circuit length used for Fig. 17 is not stated next to the figure and must be inferred or disclosed as a fitted discrete parameter.

cards.title: Cavity-filtered frequency-noise projection

source_refs.value: Fig. 12: projected filtering by a cavity with 140 kHz linewidth

cards.role: Reproduces the cavity-transfer calculation used by the FRT projection in Fig. 12(a).

checks.reason: The target paper specifies a 140 kHz cavity filter; the single-pole transfer convention is explicitly marked reconstructed.
The filter leaves the dc component unchanged.
The projected PSD is suppressed quadratically above the cavity linewidth.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the disclosed single-pole power transfer. An absolute paper-specific infidelity projection additionally requires the unpublished numerical PSD and is marked blocked.
open_questions: The paper does not print the exact cavity transfer convention used for the projection.
